pending_commit.commit_message: BACKPORT: Add udmabuf misc device A driver to let userspace turn memfd regions into dma-bufs. Use case: Allows qemu create dmabufs for the vga framebuffer or virtio-gpu ressources. Then they can be passed around to display those guest things on the host. To spice client for classic full framebuffer display, and hopefully some day to wayland server for seamless guest window display. qemu test branch: https://git.kraxel.org/cgit/qemu/log/?h=sirius/udmabuf Cc: David Airlie <airlied@linux.ie> Cc: Tomeu Vizoso <tomeu.vizoso@collabora.com> Cc: Laurent Pinchart <laurent.pinchart@ideasonboard.com> Cc: Daniel Vetter <daniel@ffwll.ch> Signed-off-by: Gerd Hoffmann <kraxel@redhat.com> Acked-by: Daniel Vetter <daniel.vetter@ffwll.ch> Link: http://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20180827093444.23623-1-kraxel@redhat.com (cherry picked from commit fbb0de795078190a9834b3409e4b009cfb18a6d4) Signed-off-by: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org> Backport notes: The following upstream commits refactored some code, and were changed back locally: f9b67f ("dma-buf: Rename dma-ops to prevent conflict with kunmap_atomic") Changed {.kmap, .kunmap} to {.map, .unmap} in struct dma_buf_ops. 11bac8 ("mm, fs: reduce fault, page_mkwrite, and pfn_mkwrite to take only vmf") Stopped passing struct vm_area_struct *vma into the page fault handler. 5aadc4 ("shmem: rename functions that are memfd-related") Changed shmem_fcntl(..) into memfd_fcntl(..). BUG=chromium:892806 TEST=compiles Change-Id: I532b74a5aadcce2b74b70d42b01568a5a9979fd6 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1265395 Tested-by: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Robert Tarasov <tutankhamen@chromium.org>

Drop udev dependency for frecon-lite This patch expands the existing frecon-lite concept that is currently only managed by ebuilds (and the DBUS=0 command line flag) to be known within the frecon Makefiles. Code that is different between the two binaries is split into separate files with _full.c/_lite.c suffix. Also decouple frecon-lite from udev so that we can drop another big dependency from the recovery initramfs. Instead frecon-lite will simply listen to all /dev/input/eventX nodes that exist on startup. We don't really care about hotplugging for recovery, and the extra power consumption from listening to irrelevant inputs doesn't really matter for that use case. BUG=chromium:984814 TEST=Ran recovery on Kevin, confirmed I could still switch VTs with Ctrl+Alt+F2. shill: connection: Update default route metrics along with policy rules Connection::SetMetric is called by Manager to inform a Connection instance of a new metric. The primary effect of this call is to modify the priority of policy routing rules. However, since the metric of a Connection also has an effect on the metric of newly-created default routes, we would like to be consistent and also update the metric of existing default routes when SetMetric is called. BUG=chromium:941597 TEST=-All unit tests are passing. -Manual testing, checking route metrics with `ip route show table 0 | grep '^default .* metric'`. platform.MemoryPressure: don't log times for discarded tabs I noticed we were getting some very low tab switch numbers occassionally for the cold tab switches and determined this was because we were trying to switch to discarded tabs but still reporting a non-zero switch time. Having some discarded tabs in that phase of the test is expected, but we shouldn't report it as a successful switch. Instead, let's report whether a tab activiation was successful or not and if not 0 for either a discarded tab or any other error. Also fix a lint error for the comment for googleLogIn(). autotest: Fix CheckInterfaceForDestination behavior CheckInterfaceForDestination is meant to ensure that the host will use the specified interface to reach particular addresses. The previous implementation used routes parsed from /proc/net/{route,ipv6_route} to perform this logic. However, not only does this preclude routes from other tables, but also ignores a large amount of logic in the kernel regarding policy routing rules and the routing cache. This change modifies the implementation to use `ip route get`, which takes all this into account. BUG=chromium:941597 TEST=`test_that $IP cellular_Smoke.fibocom-l850gl` now passes. Change-Id: I610c67dfdef6d488c6e847050d494eb273224907 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1719094 Tested-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Eric Caruso <ejcaruso@chromium.org>

shill: routing_table_entry: Remove from_rtnl field Previously, the from_rtnl field was set when a route was learned about by listening to rtnl messages (rather than coming from a client within shill). This distinction provides little value, and the code currently performs no useful logic with regards to whether or not the field is set. The primary user of from_rtnl is test code, which explicitly sets from_rtnl to fake that a RoutingTableEntry came from RoutingTable::ParseRoutingTableMessage. If in the future we would like to distinguish between routes from different clients or for different purposes, the protocol field would be a more useful, appropriate, and kernel/rtnl-supported means of doing so. BUG=None TEST=All unit tests are passing. cbfs: Avoid buffer over/underrun in cbfs_get_header cbfs_get_header() was simply trusting the offset inside of the buf, and using that to point to another region in the buffer. If something is wrong with that data, then get_cbfs_header() will reach through wild values and crash. Specifically if the buffer ends up being zeroed out, then get_cbfs_header() reaches about 4GB below the buffer. Do some initial boundary checking on the header ptr before reaching through it.
